name: Computer Science, BS
degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

requirements.title: Required Introductory Courses
requirements.sourceText: CSE 113 - Foundations of Computer Science I OR CSE 150 - Foundations of Computer Science: Honors; CSE 114 - Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming; CSE 213 - Foundations of Computer Science II; CSE 214 - Data Structures; CSE 220 - Systems Fundamentals I

requirements.title: Required Advanced Courses
requirements.sourceText: CSE 307 - Principles of Programming Languages; CSE 316 - Fundamentals of Software Development; CSE 320 - Systems Fundamentals II; CSE 373 - Analysis of Algorithms OR CSE 385 - Analysis of Algorithms: Honors; CSE 356 - Cloud Computing OR CSE 416 - Software Engineering. Note: CSE 356 or CSE 416 must be completed at Stony Brook University.

requirements.title: Computer Science Electives
requirements.sourceText: Six additional upper-division technical CSE courses, each of which must carry at least three credits. Courses used to satisfy the required advanced courses requirement may not be used to satisfy the computer science electives requirement. Technical electives do not include teaching practica (CSE 475), the first part of the senior honors project (CSE 495), and courses designated as non-technical in the course description (such as CSE 301). Students may only use 3 credits from the following courses to satisfy one upper-division technical elective for the CSE major requirements: CSE 487, CSE 496, VIP 395, VIP 396, VIP 495, VIP 496.

requirements.title: Calculus sequence
requirements.sourceText: One of the following calculus course sequences: AMS 151, AMS 161; MAT 125, MAT 126, MAT 127; MAT 131, MAT 132. Equivalency for MAT courses achieved through the Mathematics Placement Examination is accepted to meet the Calculus course requirements.

requirements.title: Linear algebra
requirements.sourceText: One of the following linear algebra courses: MAT 211 - Introduction to Linear Algebra; AMS 210 - Applied Linear Algebra

requirements.title: Required Upper-Division Statistics Course
requirements.sourceText: AMS 310 - Survey of Probability and Statistics

requirements.title: Science lecture/laboratory combination
requirements.sourceText: At least one of the following science lecture/laboratory combinations: BIO 201 + BIO 204; BIO 202 + BIO 204; BIO 203 + BIO 204; CHE 131 + CHE 133; CHE 152 + CHE 154; PHY 126 + PHY 133; PHY 131 + PHY 133; PHY 141 + PHY 133

requirements.title: Additional natural science course
requirements.sourceText: One additional natural science course selected from below. Note: One may not take science courses that are deemed equivalent to satisfy 7 and 8 (e.g., PHY 125 and PHY 131).

requirements.title: Required Non-Technical Courses
requirements.sourceText: CSE 300 - Technical Communications; CSE 312 - Social, Legal, and Ethical Issues in Computing

policies.sourceText: All courses taken to satisfy Requirements 1 through 9 must be taken for a letter grade.
The courses in Requirements 1-6, and 9 must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher.
The grade point average for the courses in Requirements 7 and 8 must be at least 2.00.
At least 24 credits from items 1 to 3 below, and at least 18 credits from items 2 and 3, must be completed at Stony Brook.
At least 24 credits from items 1 to 3 below, and at least 18 credits from items 2 and 3, must be completed at Stony Brook.
Note: CSE 356 or CSE 416 must be completed at Stony Brook University.
To enroll in CSE courses, students must: Have completed all prerequisites with a grade of C or higher. (Pass/No Credit grades are not acceptable to meet prerequisites.)

substitutions.sourceText: Note: Students may substitute the four courses CSE 160, CSE 161, CSE 260 and CSE 261 for the three courses CSE 114, CSE 214 and CSE 307.
Students pursuing Honors may substitute CSE 350 - Theory of Computation: Honors for CSE 213.

with.text: Senior design (440/441) in ECE, ESE or MEC, provided that the design project contains a significant software component
with.reason: The page gives course numbers but not subject codes, and eligibility depends on project content

substitutions.condition: Students double majoring with ECE, ESE or MEC
substitutions.sourceText: In Requirement 2 above, students who are double majoring with ECE, ESE or MEC may substitute their senior design (440/441) for CSE 356 - Cloud Computing or CSE 416 - Software Engineering provided that the design project contains a significant software component. Approval of the Department of Computer Science is required.

exemptions.reason: CEAS majors are exempt from the LANG learning objective.

notes.text: Students outside the major are admitted after completing CSE 113, CSE 114, and CSE 214 with grades of B- or higher and a 3.00 GPA in those courses, repeating at most one of them, with a cumulative GPA of 3.00 or higher. Applications are due January 5 (Spring) and June 5 (Fall).
The Pass/No Credit option is not available for CSE courses.
Equivalency for MAT courses achieved through the Mathematics Placement Examination is accepted to meet the Calculus course requirements.
Students may satisfy the Pursue Deeper Understanding category of the SBC by completing CSE 316 and CSE 416. An SBS+ or HFA+ course is required for students who complete CSE 356 in lieu of CSE 416.
All students are encouraged to discuss their program with an undergraduate advisor.
